transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Hi Ms. Oyelaran, I'm Dr. Sallow. What brings you in?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: An itchy rash on the inside of my elbows and behind my knees. It's been about two months.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Have you had anything like it before?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I had eczema as a kid, but it went away. The itching is worst at night.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Over-the-counter hydrocortisone 1 percent cream. It helps a little for a day or two.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Any new soaps, detergents, or lotions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I started a scented body wash around when it began. And I'm a barista, so I wash my hands constantly.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Any other health problems or medicines?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Seasonal allergies. I take loratadine 10 mg in the spring. No other medicines.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Anyone in the family with eczema, asthma, or hay fever?

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: On exam, there are red, thickened plaques with scratch marks on both inner elbows and behind both knees. There's no oozing, crusting, or pus. The hands show mild dryness. The rest of the skin is clear.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: This is atopic dermatitis, a flare of eczema, probably made worse by the scented body wash and frequent handwashing. I'm prescribing triamcinolone 0.1 percent ointment twice a day to the elbows and knees for two weeks, then stop. Don't use it on your face.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Switch to a fragrance-free cleanser, take lukewarm showers, and put on a thick fragrance-free moisturizer right after bathing and after handwashing. Let's see you back in four weeks.

sections.title: Chief complaint
sections.text: Itchy rash on the inner elbows and behind the knees for about two months.

sections.title: History of present illness
sections.text: Itchy rash on the inside of both elbows and behind both knees for about two months; itching worst at night. Eczema as a child that went away. Over-the-counter hydrocortisone 1 percent cream helps a little for a day or two. Started a scented body wash around when the rash began. Works as a barista and washes her hands constantly.

sections.title: Past medical history
sections.text: Childhood eczema. Seasonal allergies, loratadine 10 mg in the spring. No other medicines.

sections.title: Physical exam
sections.text: Red, thickened plaques with scratch marks on both inner elbows and behind both knees. No oozing, crusting, or pus. Mild dryness of the hands. Rest of the skin clear.

sections.title: Assessment and plan
sections.text: Atopic dermatitis, eczema flare, probably made worse by the scented body wash and frequent handwashing. Triamcinolone 0.1 percent ointment twice a day to the elbows and knees for two weeks, then stop; not on the face. Fragrance-free cleanser, lukewarm showers, thick fragrance-free moisturizer after bathing and handwashing. Follow-up in four weeks.

sections.title: Patient instructions
sections.text: Apply triamcinolone 0.1 percent ointment twice a day to the elbows and knees for two weeks, then stop. Don't use it on your face. Switch to a fragrance-free cleanser, take lukewarm showers, and put on a thick fragrance-free moisturizer right after bathing and after handwashing. Return in four weeks.

mustNotInvent.description: No systemic or biologic treatment was discussed.
No biopsy or patch testing was done.
Psoriasis and infection were not diagnosed.
